submission.justification: Module-D3 at 30% wall coverage achieves the highest light collection of 52.54 PE/MeV, significantly outperforming Module-D1 (39.67 PE/MeV) and Module-D2 (23.97 PE/MeV) at the same coverage. The large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter design provides superior photon detection efficiency. At 30% coverage, we maximize performance within the allowed constraints while utilizing the available feedthrough capacity confirmed in the 2026-01-20 meeting. Cold electronics have been validated for all candidate designs, including Module-D3. This configuration delivers 32% better light collection than Module-D1 and 119% better than Module-D2 at maximum coverage, providing the best physics sensitivity for the neutrino experiment.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV)
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 at 30% coverage achieves 52.54 PE/MeV, the highest value among all tested configurations across all three module designs and all coverage levels tested.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter) is one of the three candidate designs listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Modules must be robust, since they are inaccessible after the cryostat is filled
requirements.evidence: Cold electronics have been validated for Module-D3 per electronics.md. No reliability concerns are mentioned in project documents for any of the three candidate designs.
Recommended coverage of 30% is within the allowed range. Meeting notes from 2026-01-20 confirm that sufficient feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.
